content: Lake Alice Hospital was a rural psychiatric facility located near Marton in Rangitikei, New Zealand. It was established in 1950 and included a Maximum Security unit. Similar to many psychiatric hospitals in New Zealand, Lake Alice was largely self-sufficient, featuring its own farm, workshop, bakery, laundry, and fire station. The hospital also had recreational facilities such as swimming pools, as well as glasshouses and vegetable gardens. The facility ceased operations in 1999. In July 2006, the buildings and the 56-hectare grounds were sold to an undisclosed buyer. During the 1970s, allegations of abuse were made by former patients of the hospital's child and adolescent unit. These allegations included the use of electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and paraldehyde injections as forms of punishment. A total of $7 million in compensation was awarded to 183 former patients. The former head of the child and adolescent unit relinquished his medical license to avoid a disciplinary hearing by the Medical Practitioners Board of Victoria.
